area: Gain rules (gainStatus, Gain exceptions in findExceptions, gainStrip chart, Yearling gain tile)
summary:
On the committed data the gain rules are correct. Heifers come out at 0.436 lbs/day and yearlings at 1.942, and the slow-animal list is the planted six. I recomputed all of these separately in Python as pooled gain divided by animal-days and they match exactly. Thresholds are strict 'under', negative gains are handled, and the page renders the tile and chart correctly.

The rule breaks easily on ordinary real-world weigh-in data. Three high-severity defects were reproduced:
(1) An animal with only one weigh-in throws inside gainStatus. findExceptions then returns nothing, and the page shows no tiles, no report and no as-of line.
(2) Two weigh-ins on the same day give a zero-day interval and an ADG of ±Infinity or NaN. NaN or +Infinity removes the serious heifer alert, and -Infinity prints '-Infinity lbs/day'. For ±Infinity, the gainStrip gridline loop never ends: the tab hangs and nothing paints. A CDP pause stack points to gainStrip at app.js:157.
(3) The tile hard-codes a group called 'Yearlings'. With no such group, no yearling weigh-ins, or a non-numeric target, tiles() throws before the exception table is drawn.

Medium defects that hide real alerts or raise false ones:
- Tags are keyed by tag alone, so the same tag in two groups merges into one animal (and also hangs the page).
- One-day re-weighs carry full weight in the average, because the group figure is a plain mean of per-animal ADGs. One 20-lb fill reading masks the heifer alert: mean 0.869 vs pooled 0.442.
- Implausible weights are not checked: a typo of 11690 masks the heifer alert and stretches the chart axis to 185.
- A blank weight is treated as 0 lbs.
- Animals that missed the last weigh-in are averaged in with stale data, which hides the six slow yearlings. The group's 'since' date comes from the first animal only.
- Weigh-in group labels that are not in groups.csv, and groups with no weigh-ins, vanish without a word.
- Dates are sorted as text, so non-ISO dates pick the wrong pair of weigh-ins.
- A non-numeric target silently turns off that group's gain alerts.

Design limits:
- Coverage (the 'head' field is the number weighed, compared with nothing).
- Stale weigh-ins are presented as current with no age shown.
- Weigh conditions (shrink and gut fill) are not recorded. A 3% difference flips both verdicts.
- Groups with a 0.0 target (the cows) are skipped and the page doesn't say so.

Low: weigh-ins dated after as_of are used; an animal that changes group is counted in its earlier group; wording says 'since Jul 20' for a period that ended Sep 15, plus '1 yearlings' and 1.598 shown as '1.60'.

All 37 cases are in docs/audit/diagnostics/gain.repro.mjs: 6 controls MATCH, 31 MISMATCH, 0 unexpected throws. That is the only file I created in the repo. No existing file was modified, and nothing was committed.
trace:
SOURCE: data/weights.csv has 585 rows (tag, group, date, weight_lbs): 45 heifers (H001-H045) and 150 yearlings (Y001-Y150), each weighed 2026-06-01, 2026-07-20 and 2026-09-15. There are no cow rows. data/groups.csv: Cows (180 head, target_adg_lbs 0.0), Heifers (45, 1.0), Yearlings (150, 2.0). meta.csv: as_of 2026-09-30T18:00.

PARSE: parseCSV (exceptions.js:22-34) turns numeric-looking cells into numbers and leaves "" or other text as strings. Tags like H001 stay strings; a purely numeric tag or date becomes a number.

gainStatus(weights, groups) (exceptions.js:64-80):
- Groups rows into a Map keyed by tag only.
- Sorts each animal's rows by date with string localeCompare.
- Takes [a, b] = rows.slice(-2), the last two rows whatever their dates or groups.
- Builds each animal as {group: a.group (the EARLIER row), from: a.date, to: b.date, adg: (b.weight_lbs - a.weight_lbs) / days(a.date, b.date), weight: b.weight_lbs}. days() is a Date difference / 864e5 with no guard for 0, NaN or a negative interval.
- Then for each groups.csv row: animals whose group string matches exactly. If there are none the group is skipped. It emits {head: number of animals weighed, target, from/to: the FIRST animal's dates, adg: plain mean of per-animal ADG, animals}.
- No as_of, no coverage against groups.csv head, no plausibility checks.

findExceptions (exceptions.js:127-138):
- Groups with a falsy target are skipped (Cows 0.0, also a blank target).
- groupLow = adg < target×0.8. If true it pushes serious | Gain | <group> | "<adg.toFixed(2)> lbs/day since <from> vs <target.toFixed(1)> target", action "Check forage quality and mineral; look for a health problem in the group".
- Otherwise, if any animal has adg < target×0.5, it pushes warning | Gain | "<n> <group lowercased>" | "Under <(0.5×target).toFixed(1)> lbs/day: <tags>", action "Pull and check these animals at the next gather".
- Rows are sorted by severity, then area.

PAGE (app.js):
- Line 222 calls findExceptions at module top level; a throw here stops everything, even the as-of line on line 223.
- Line 225 renders in order: tiles → exceptionsTable → waterMultiples → grazingTimeline → gainStrip → budget → rules.
- tiles() (48, 56) does gainStatus(...).find(g => g.group === "Yearlings") and prints "Yearling gain / <adg.toFixed(2)> lbs/day / target <target.toFixed(1)>, since <fmtDate(from)>". A throw here leaves the exception table empty.
- gainStrip() (149-176) keeps groups with a truthy target. The axis runs from lo = min(0, floor(2·min ADG)/2) to hi = ceil(2·max(ADGs, targets))/2, with a gridline loop `for (v = lo; v <= hi + 1e-9; v += 0.5)`. That loop never ends if hi = +Infinity or lo = -Infinity, and a NaN skips it. Each animal is one jittered dot, with an 'avg' label and a target line; the tooltip shows tag, ADG, from-to, current weight and "Under half of target".

COMMITTED-DATA RESULT (GN-C1/C2, GB-C1; checked separately in Python):
- Heifers: 1119 lbs over 2565 animal-days = 0.436257, giving "Serious | Gain | Heifers | 0.44 lbs/day since 2026-07-20 vs 1.0 target". 32 heifers are under 0.5, but they are not listed, as documented.
- Yearlings: 16608 / 8550 = 1.942456, so no group row. Y027, Y031, Y058, Y082, Y129 and Y132 are under 1.0, giving "Warning | Gain | 6 yearlings | Under 1.0 lbs/day: Y027, Y031, Y058, Y082, Y129, Y132".
- Tile: "Yearling gain / 1.94 lbs/day / target 2.0, since Jul 20".
- Chart: 195 dots, gridlines 0.0 to 3.0, labels avg 0.44 / target 1.0 / avg 1.94 / target 2.0.
- The existing tests (8/8 pass) cover only these planted outcomes and head counts [45, 150]. None covers a single weigh-in, duplicates, missing groups or bad values.

findings.title: An animal with a single weigh-in crashes findExceptions; the page shows no alerts at all
findings.location: exceptions.js:69-70 (const [a, b] = rows.slice(-2); ... b.date); app.js:222 (findExceptions at module top level)
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/gain.repro.mjs, cases GN-01, GN-02 and GB-01. Committed weights plus one row 'Y151,Yearlings,2026-09-15,820' (a new purchase weighed once). GN-02 instead adds 'C017,Cows,2026-09-15,1310' (a cow, which is never judged on gain).
findings.expected: No throw. All 10 committed alerts are returned. Y151 is left out of the gain figures, or listed as 'first weigh-in, no gain yet'.
findings.actual: GN-01/GN-02: "threw TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'date')". GB-01: "pageerrors=[\"Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'date')\"]; asof=\"\"; tiles=0; exception rows=0; gain chart=false"
findings.consequence: One newly bought, replacement or cull animal weighed once wipes the whole dashboard. The leaking tank, the overdue booster and the budget overrun all disappear, and nothing says why. This is a crash that hides every alert, triggered by the most common kind of real weigh-in file.
findings.regression_test: Load the committed data, append {tag:'Y151', group:'Yearlings', date:'2026-09-15', weight_lbs:820}, and call findExceptions. Assert no throw and length === 10. Assert gainStatus(...).find(Yearlings).adg is about 16608/8550 = 1.94246, worked out by hand from the Jul 20 and Sep 15 weights, so Y151 is excluded. Optionally assert Y151 appears in a 'not yet re-weighed' list.
findings.proposed_fix: In gainStatus, skip animals with fewer than 2 usable rows and return them as notReweighed: [...]. In app.js, wrap each section (findExceptions, tiles, each chart) in try/catch so one failing section shows an inline error and doesn't blank the report.

findings.title: A zero-day interval (same-day duplicate weigh-in) gives ±Infinity/NaN ADG: the alert is lost or garbled, and the page hangs
findings.location: exceptions.js:36 and 70 (division by days(a.date,b.date) = 0); app.js:152-158 (axis from Math.min/Math.max of the ADGs; gridline for-loop with no bound)
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/gain.repro.mjs, cases GN-04/05/06 and GB-04/07/08. Committed weights plus a second Sep 15 row for H001 (a re-weigh after re-zeroing the scale): 'H001,Heifers,2026-09-15,1180' gives +Infinity, 1169 gives NaN, 1160 gives -Infinity.
findings.expected: The duplicate is collapsed or flagged. Heifers stay 'serious ... 0.44 lbs/day'. No Infinity or NaN appears anywhere, and the page renders within a few seconds.
findings.actual: GN-04 (+Inf): "Heifers adg=Infinity ... warning | 32 heifers | Under 0.5 lbs/day: H002, ..." (the serious row is gone). GN-05 (NaN): "Heifers adg=NaN", the same downgrade. GN-06: "serious | Heifers | -Infinity lbs/day since 2026-09-15 vs 1.0 target". GB-04 (NaN): "dots=195 (NaN cx: 195) gridlines=0 labels=[\"avg NaN\",...]". GB-07/GB-08: "PAGE HUNG: main thread did not answer page.evaluate within 2.5 s; screenshot timed out (nothing painted); paused stack: svg (app.js:12) <- gainStrip (app.js:157) <- (module top level) (app.js:225)"
findings.consequence: A routine scale re-check silently downgrades a group-wide gain problem to an individual-animal warning (NaN or +Infinity case), or prints '-Infinity lbs/day'. In the ±Infinity cases the browser tab freezes before anything paints, so the manager sees a blank, unresponsive page with no alerts. The tab's memory also kept growing: free memory fell about 270 MB in 3 s. That is observed; that the tab would eventually crash is my inference.
findings.regression_test: Committed data plus {H001, Heifers, 2026-09-15, 1180}. Assert every animal's adg is finite. Assert a serious Heifers row whose problem starts '0.44'. By hand: keeping the first reading gives 1119/2565 = 0.4363; keeping the later one gives (1119-31+42)/2565 = 1130/2565 = 0.4405; both show 0.44. Browser test: the page reaches '#rules tr' within 2 s and the gain chart has 7 gridlines.
findings.proposed_fix: Dedupe rows by (tag, date): keep the last reading and report the duplicate. Require a minimum interval, for example at least 14 days, before computing ADG. Drop non-finite values with Number.isFinite before averaging. In gainStrip, build the axis only from finite values, and bound the loop (for example `for (let i = 0; i <= Math.min(40, (hi-lo)/0.5); i++)`).

findings.title: The Yearling tile hard-codes a group named 'Yearlings'; when it's missing, tiles() throws before the report is drawn
findings.location: app.js:48 (.find((g) => g.group === "Yearlings")), app.js:56 (gain.adg, gain.target.toFixed), app.js:225 (tiles runs before exceptionsTable)
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/gain.repro.mjs, cases GB-02, GB-03 and GB-06. GB-02: rename Yearlings to Steers in both groups.csv and weights.csv. GB-03: weights.csv with no yearling rows yet. GB-06: yearling target keyed as '2.O'.
findings.expected: No page error. The exception table is drawn (10 rows for GB-02, 9 for GB-03). The gain tile shows another group or says 'no yearling weigh-ins yet'.
findings.actual: GB-02 and GB-03: "pageerrors=[\"Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'adg')\"]; ... tiles=0; exception rows=0; gain chart=false". GB-06: "pageerrors=[\"gain.target.toFixed is not a function\"]; ... tiles=0; exception rows=0"
findings.consequence: The README invites ranches to 'replace the CSVs with exports in the same columns'. Any ranch whose group isn't spelled exactly 'Yearlings' (steers, feeders, stockers, a cow-calf-only outfit), or whose yearlings haven't been re-weighed yet, gets a page with headings and no exception report. This crash hides all alerts.
findings.regression_test: Browser test against a scratch copy, with groups.csv and weights.csv rewritten from Yearlings to Steers. Assert no pageerror, '#exceptions tr' count = 11 (header plus 10, matching the committed data), and a tile that doesn't say 'undefined'. Also: weights filtered to heifers only gives header plus 9 rows (the committed 10 minus the 6-yearling warning).
findings.proposed_fix: Choose the tile group from the data (for example the group with the highest target that has weigh-ins), or show 'No gain data' when find() returns undefined. Validate that the target is numeric. Render exceptionsTable before tiles, and put each section in its own try/catch.

findings.title: Animals are keyed by tag alone, so the same tag number in two groups merges into one 'animal'
findings.location: exceptions.js:65-66 (byTag keyed on r.tag only); exceptions.js:70 (group from row a)
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/gain.repro.mjs, cases GN-17 and GB-09. weights: '101,Heifers,2026-07-20,1100 / 101,Heifers,2026-09-15,1130 / 101,Yearlings,2026-07-20,800 / 101,Yearlings,2026-09-15,910'.
findings.expected: Two animals: heifer 101 at 30/57 = 0.5263 lbs/day and yearling 101 at 110/57 = 1.9298. Or a 'duplicate tag 101 in Heifers and Yearlings' data row.
findings.actual: GN-17: "Heifers: 101 adg=-Infinity 2026-09-15..2026-09-15" (the yearling disappears). GB-09: "PAGE HUNG ... paused stack: svg (app.js:12) <- gainStrip (app.js:157)"
findings.consequence: Many ranches reuse numeric tag series across groups, telling them apart by tag color. Merged records produce nonsense ADGs, mislabelled animals and, through the zero-interval bug, a frozen page. parseCSV also turns '0101' and '101' into the same number 101.
findings.regression_test: With the four rows above, assert gainStatus returns Heifers with one animal at about 0.5263 and Yearlings with one animal at about 1.9298 (both by hand: 30/57 and 110/57). Or assert a data-quality row naming tag 101, with no non-finite ADG.
findings.proposed_fix: Detect a tag that appears in more than one group on the same weigh date and report it as a data error. Recommend a unique animal ID (EID, or tag plus color or year) in the CSV spec. Keep tags as strings in parseCSV for the tag column.

findings.title: No minimum interval, and the group figure is a plain mean of per-animal ADG: one short re-weigh masks a group-wide problem
findings.location: exceptions.js:69-70 (last two rows, whatever the gap), exceptions.js:76-77 (unweighted mean of adg)
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/gain.repro.mjs, cases GN-07 and GN-C2. Committed weights plus 'H001,Heifers,2026-09-16,1189': a next-morning re-weigh 20 lbs heavier after drinking, about 1.7% of body weight.
findings.expected: Heifers stay serious. For the Jul 20 to Sep 15 weigh period, pooled 1119/2565 = 0.436. Even pooled over each animal's last two rows it is (1119-31+20)/(44×57+1) = 0.4416.
findings.actual: "Heifers adg=0.8686 (H001 20 lbs/day over 2026-09-15..2026-09-16) || warning | 32 heifers | Under 0.5 lbs/day: ..." The serious group row is gone. Control GN-C2: when all animals share one period, mean equals pooled ("Heifers ... adg=0.4363", "Yearlings ... adg=1.9425", the same as 1119/2565 and 16608/8550).
findings.consequence: A re-weigh, or a chute-side weight on a treated animal a day or two after the main weigh-in, turns gut fill into lbs/day. One animal can lift or sink a group verdict. Here the planted heifer problem becomes an individual-animal warning (missed alert); a negative fill swing would raise a false serious alarm.
findings.regression_test: Committed data plus {H001, Heifers, 2026-09-16, 1189}. Assert a serious Heifers row whose adg is 0.43-0.45 (hand: 1119/2565 = 0.4363 over the Jul 20 to Sep 15 event pair). Assert H001's Sep 16 reading is reported as a short-interval re-weigh, not used.
findings.proposed_fix: Compute the group figure over the group's last two weigh events: dates on which most of the group crossed the scale. Use pooled gain, Σ(w_last − w_prev) / Σ days. Require at least about 21 days between the two events, and list off-event rows separately.

findings.title: No plausibility check on weights or ADG: one typo masks the heifer alert and wrecks the gain chart's scale
findings.location: exceptions.js:70 and 77; app.js:152-158 (axis spans every ADG)
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/gain.repro.mjs, cases GN-08 and GB-05. H001's Sep 15 weight keyed as 11690 instead of 1169.
findings.expected: H001 flagged as a data error (185 lbs/day is impossible). Heifers stay serious at (1119-31)/(44×57) = 1088/2508 = 0.4338. The chart axis stays 0.0 to 3.0 (7 gridlines).
findings.actual: GN-08: "Heifers adg=4.538 || warning | 32 heifers | Under 0.5 lbs/day: ...". GB-05: "gridlines=372 labels=[\"avg 4.54\",...]; target line x=[\"76.544474393531\",\"79.088948787062\"]; dot x min/median/max=[74.3,78.7,545] of a 74..546 plot"
findings.consequence: One keying slip turns a serious group alert into a long animal list, which is a missed alert. The chart shows 'avg 4.54', and all the real dots, with both target lines, crowd into about 5 px of a 472-px plot under 372 overlapping labels. A typo on the low side, for example 116 for 1160, would instead raise a false alarm for a healthy animal.
findings.regression_test: Committed data with H001's Sep 15 weight set to 11690. Assert a data-error row naming H001 (by hand: (11690−1138)/57 = 185.1 lbs/day). Assert a serious Heifers row at 0.43 (1088/2508 = 0.4338). Browser: gain chart gridline count = 7.
findings.proposed_fix: Reject weights outside a plausible range for the class (for example 200-2,500 lbs) and per-animal ADG outside, say, −3 to +6 lbs/day. List them as data errors and exclude them from group figures and the chart axis.

findings.title: A blank weight cell is treated as 0 lbs and creates a false 'pull this animal' alert
findings.location: exceptions.js:29-30 ("" kept as a string), exceptions.js:70 ("" - 711 coerces to -711)
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/gain.repro.mjs, case GN-09. The weights.csv line 'Y001,Yearlings,2026-09-15,851' changed to 'Y001,Yearlings,2026-09-15,' (the scale didn't record).
findings.expected: The blank row is skipped and flagged as missing. The slow list stays the planted six. Yearlings without Y001: (16608−140)/(149×57) = 16468/8493 = 1.939.
findings.actual: "Y001 adg=-12.4737 weight=\"\" || ... warning | 7 yearlings | Under 1.0 lbs/day: Y001, Y027, Y031, Y058, Y082, Y129, Y132"
findings.consequence: The crew is told to pull and check Y001, a normal animal, because of a missed scale reading. The tooltip would show 'Now  lbs'. A few blanks in a small group can drag the group below 80% and raise a false serious alert.
findings.regression_test: Parse the committed weights with Y001's Sep 15 weight blank. Assert the slow list is exactly [Y027, Y031, Y058, Y082, Y129, Y132]. Assert Y001 appears in a missing-weight list. If Y001 is excluded, yearling adg is about 1.939 (16468/8493, by hand).
findings.proposed_fix: Treat any non-finite weight_lbs as missing. Skip the row and report it. A shared CSV validation step should do this for every numeric column.

findings.title: Animals that missed the last weigh-in are averaged in with stale ADGs, and the group's 'since' date comes from the first animal only
findings.location: exceptions.js:69 (per-animal last two rows), exceptions.js:76 (from: mine[0].from, to: mine[0].to)
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/gain.repro.mjs, cases GN-11a and GN-11b. (a) Drop H001's Sep 15 row. (b) Drop the Sep 15 rows of the six slow yearlings, as if they were in a hospital pen at the gather.
findings.expected: (a) 'since 2026-07-20' (or 'Jul 20 to Sep 15'), with H001 noted as not weighed Sep 15; adg 1088/2508 = 0.43. (b) A Gain row naming Y027, Y031, Y058, Y082, Y129 and Y132 as not weighed Sep 15.
findings.actual: (a) "Heifers from=2026-06-01 to=2026-07-20 adg=0.4414 || serious | Heifers | 0.44 lbs/day since 2026-06-01 vs 1.0 target". (b) "the six now: Y027 2.0816 (2026-06-01..2026-07-20), ... Y132 1.6122 (2026-06-01..2026-07-20) || serious | Heifers | ..." No yearling row at all.
findings.consequence: (b) is a missed alert. The poor-doers, who are often exactly the animals absent from a gather, are judged on their early-summer gain and disappear from the report, and nothing says six head weren't weighed. (a) One absent animal changes the date printed on the whole group's alert, to a period 44 of 45 heifers weren't measured over.
findings.regression_test: (b) Committed data minus the six slow yearlings' Sep 15 rows. Assert a Gain row that includes 'Y027' and says they missed the Sep 15 weigh-in. (a) Committed data minus H001's Sep 15 row. Assert the heifer row mentions 2026-07-20 (or 'Jul 20'), not 2026-06-01, with adg 0.43 (1088/2508, by hand).
findings.proposed_fix: Find the group's latest weigh event. Compute the group figure only for animals weighed at both of the last two events. List animals missing from the latest event in their own row. Take from/to from the event dates, not from mine[0].

findings.title: Weigh-in rows or groups that don't line up with groups.csv vanish without a trace
findings.location: exceptions.js:73-75 (loop over groups.csv; exact string match; `if (!mine.length) continue`)
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/gain.repro.mjs, cases GN-15 and GN-03. GN-15: the six slow yearlings' rows keyed with group 'yearlings' (lower case). GN-03: all Heifers rows missing from weights.csv.
findings.expected: GN-15: a data row naming the unknown group 'yearlings' (6 animals), or a case-insensitive match that keeps the '6 yearlings' warning. GN-03: 'Heifers: no weigh-ins on record (45 head, target 1.0)'.
findings.actual: GN-15: "Yearlings head=144 adg=1.9998 || serious | Heifers | 0.44 ..." (the slow-animal warning is gone). GN-03: "gainStatus: Yearlings: head=150 ... || Gain rows: warning | 6 yearlings | ..." (no mention of heifers).
findings.consequence: A capitalisation slip, a trailing space or a group renamed mid-season silently removes animals from the report (a missed alert). A group that wasn't weighed looks the same as a group with no problem (a misleading all-clear).
findings.regression_test: GN-15 data: assert a row that includes 'yearlings' as an unknown group (6 animals), or a '6 yearlings' warning that names Y027. GN-03 data: assert a Gain row whose subject contains 'Heifers' and says no weigh-ins.
findings.proposed_fix: After grouping, report every weights.csv group label not in groups.csv. For every groups.csv group with a target and no usable weigh-ins, emit a 'no current weigh-in' warning.

findings.title: Weigh-in dates are sorted and parsed as text: non-ISO dates use the wrong pair, and numeric dates crash
findings.location: exceptions.js:68 (rows.sort((a, b) => a.date.localeCompare(b.date))); exceptions.js:30 (numeric-looking dates become numbers)
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/gain.repro.mjs, case GN-16. Y001 rows dated 6/1/2026, 7/20/2026, 9/15/2026 and 10/12/2026 (a US-locale spreadsheet export with a fall weigh-in). Also compact dates 20260720 and 20260915.
findings.expected: Latest pair Sep 15 (851) to Oct 12 (880): 29/27 = 1.0741 lbs/day, current weight 880. Or a 'dates must be YYYY-MM-DD' data error. Compact dates: no throw.
findings.actual: "US dates: Y001 from 7/20/2026 to 9/15/2026, adg 2.4561, weight 851 || compact dates: threw TypeError: a.date.localeCompare is not a function"
findings.consequence: After a re-export in another date format, the dashboard silently judges an older period and ignores the newest weigh-in, or crashes everything (see the single-weigh-in finding for what a crash does). The README doesn't specify a date format.
findings.regression_test: With the four US-dated rows, assert either a data-format error or from = Oct 12's predecessor (Sep 15), to = 10/12/2026, adg about 1.0741 (29/27 by hand), weight 880. With compact dates, assert no throw.
findings.proposed_fix: Validate the date column as YYYY-MM-DD at load time, report bad rows, and sort by parsed timestamps. Document the required format in the README.

findings.title: A non-numeric target silently disables a group's gain alerts (and crashes the tile)
findings.location: exceptions.js:128-133 ("2.O" * 0.8 = NaN, so every comparison is false); app.js:56 and 173 (target.toFixed)
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/gain.repro.mjs, cases GN-20 and GB-06. groups.csv Yearlings target '2.O' (letter O). In GN-20 the yearlings' Sep 15 weights are set to Jul 20 + 50 lbs, which is 50/57 = 0.877 lbs/day.
findings.expected: A data-error row for the bad target, or the yearlings judged serious at 0.88.
findings.actual: GN-20: "Yearlings adg=0.8772 target=\"2.O\" || serious | Heifers | 0.44 ..." (no yearling row). GB-06: "pageerrors=[\"gain.target.toFixed is not a function\"]; ... exception rows=0"
findings.consequence: A single keying slip in a configuration file turns off gain alerting for the main group (a missed alert). In the browser it also blanks the report.
findings.regression_test: Committed data with groups.csv Yearlings target '2.O'. Assert a data row naming the Yearlings target, and that the page renders the exception table.
findings.proposed_fix: Validate that groups.csv target_adg_lbs and head are finite numbers ≥ 0, and report bad rows as data errors. Treat an invalid target as 'not judged (bad target)', never silently.

findings.title: No coverage or sample-size check: a group verdict can rest on a handful of animals, undisclosed
findings.location: exceptions.js:76 (head: mine.length, the number weighed, never compared with groups.csv head); exceptions.js:129-131 (no n in the text); app.js:56 (tile has no n)
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/gain.repro.mjs, case GN-13. Only Y001-Y003 weighed (700 then 785.5 lbs = 1.50 lbs/day); groups.csv says 150 head.
findings.expected: The row says '3 of 150 weighed', or the rule declines to judge below a minimum coverage.
findings.actual: "gainStatus Yearlings head=3 (groups.csv head=150) || serious | Yearlings | 1.50 lbs/day since 2026-07-20 vs 2.0 target"
findings.consequence: A manager could act on, for example by changing supplement for the whole group, a verdict drawn from 2% of the group, with no way to tell from the report. The reverse also holds: a reassuring average from a few animals hides the rest. The field name 'head' means 'animals weighed', which reads like the herd count.
findings.regression_test: GN-13 data: assert the Yearlings row contains '3 of 150', or is replaced by a 'too few weighed (3 of 150)' warning. On the committed data, assert '45 of 45' and '150 of 150', or no disclosure needed because coverage is 100%.
findings.proposed_fix: Pass groups.csv head into the gain summary. Show 'n of head weighed' in the alert, tile and chart label. Set a minimum (for example at least 50% of head and at least 10 animals) below which the rule reports 'insufficient weigh-in coverage' instead of a verdict. Rename head to weighed.

findings.title: Stale weigh-ins are presented as current: no age check, and an all-clear based on 72-day-old data
findings.location: exceptions.js:127-138 (no comparison with as_of); app.js:56 (tile shows only the start date)
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/gain.repro.mjs, case GN-18. All Sep 15 rows removed, so the latest period is Jun 1 to Jul 20; as_of is still 2026-09-30.
findings.expected: A row or note saying the last weigh-in was Jul 20, 72 days before the as-of date (Jul 20 to Sep 30: 11 + 31 + 30 = 72 days).
findings.actual: "Heifers: head=45 adg=0.917 from=2026-06-01 to=2026-07-20; Yearlings: head=150 adg=1.9807 ... || warning | 4 heifers | Under 0.5 lbs/day: H014, H017, H025, H033" The warning row carries no date at all.
findings.consequence: If a weigh-in is skipped or not exported, the report quietly judges an old period. Here the serious heifer slump vanishes and a small early-summer warning takes its place: a misleading all-clear.
findings.regression_test: GN-18 data: assert a Gain row stating the last weigh-in date (2026-07-20) and its age of 72 days (hand count). On the committed data (Sep 15, 15 days old) assert no staleness row if the limit is, for example, 45 days.
findings.proposed_fix: Add RULES.weighStaleDays, for example 45. Emit a warning when a judged group's latest weigh-in is older than that. Always print both weigh dates in the gain rows and the tile.

findings.title: Weigh conditions (shrink and gut fill) aren't recorded; an ordinary 3% difference flips both group verdicts
findings.location: weights.csv schema (tag, group, date, weight_lbs only); scripts/generate_data.py:140; exceptions.js:129 (0.8 × target margin)
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/gain.repro.mjs, case GN-19. Yearlings' Sep 15 weights × 0.97 (shrunk after an overnight stand); heifers' Sep 15 weights × 1.03 (full). The 3% figure is my assumption of an ordinary shrink/fill swing, not a measured value.
findings.expected: With consistent conditions the verdicts would be unchanged: yearlings no serious row, heifers serious. Separately computed: 1.4973 and 1.0203 under the perturbation.
findings.actual: "Heifers: head=45 adg=1.0203 ...; Yearlings: head=150 adg=1.4973 ... || serious | Yearlings | 1.50 lbs/day since 2026-07-20 vs 2.0 target" The planted heifer alert is gone, and a false yearling alert appears.
findings.consequence: The serious rule's margin (0.4 lbs/day for yearlings, 0.2 for heifers) is smaller than the ADG error a few percent of fill difference makes over a 57-day period: about 0.45 lbs/day on an 847-lb yearling. Without the conditions recorded, the rule can't tell a real gain problem from a weigh-day difference.
findings.regression_test: After the data-model change: weights with a condition column (full or shrunk, or hours off feed and water). Assert a pair with mismatched conditions is flagged, or adjusted by a stated pencil shrink before the ADG is judged.
findings.proposed_fix: Add weigh-condition columns (time off feed and water, scale) to weights.csv. Apply a consistent pencil shrink or flag mismatched pairs. Say on the page that gain is compared at the stated conditions.

findings.title: Groups with a 0.0 target (cows) are skipped silently in the report and the chart
findings.location: exceptions.js:128 (`if (!g.target) continue`); app.js:150 (.filter((g) => g.target)); app.js:209-210 and README rules table (no mention)
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/gain.repro.mjs, case GN-14. Five cows weighed at 1300 lbs on Jul 20 and 1215 on Sep 15: −85/57 = −1.49 lbs/day.
findings.expected: Either a maintenance rule (for example flag a loss beyond some lbs/day) or a visible note that groups without a gain target aren't judged.
findings.actual: "gainStatus Cows adg=-1.4912 target=0 || serious | Heifers | ... || warning | 6 yearlings | ..." No cow row, and cows are absent from the chart. The rules table and the chart note ('One dot per animal; the line is the group's target.') say nothing about it.
findings.consequence: Cows losing condition while nursing, a real concern for the rebreeding the herd depends on, would never show. A viewer can't tell whether cows were judged and passed or weren't judged at all.
findings.regression_test: Assert the rules table (app.js rules()) includes a line saying groups without a gain target are not judged. If a maintenance rule is added, GN-14 data gives a Cows row at −1.49 lbs/day (−85/57 by hand).
findings.proposed_fix: Add a line to the rules table, README and chart note. Optionally add RULES.maintenanceLoss (for example −0.5 lbs/day) for target-0 groups.

findings.title: Weigh-ins dated after as_of are used, and their date becomes the group's 'since' date
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/gain.repro.mjs, case GN-12. Committed weights plus 'H001,Heifers,2026-10-15,1200'; as_of is 2026-09-30T18:00.
findings.expected: The row is ignored or flagged. Problem: '0.44 lbs/day since 2026-07-20 vs 1.0 target'.
findings.actual: "Heifers from=2026-09-15 to=2026-10-15 || serious | Heifers | 0.45 lbs/day since 2026-09-15 vs 1.0 target"
findings.consequence: The page says 'Data as of September 30' while the figures include later data (or a mistyped year or month), and the alert names the wrong period.
findings.regression_test: GN-12 data: assert the heifer problem is exactly '0.44 lbs/day since 2026-07-20 vs 1.0 target' (or the new wording with Jul 20 to Sep 15), plus a data row noting 1 weigh-in after the as-of date.
findings.proposed_fix: Pass asOf into gainStatus, drop rows with date > asOf.slice(0,10), and report them.

findings.title: An animal that changes group between weigh-ins is counted in its earlier group
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/gain.repro.mjs, case GN-10. H001's Sep 15 row has group 'Cows' (sorted into the cow herd at preg check).
findings.expected: H001 attributed to her current group (Cows), or the change flagged. Heifers: 44 weighed, adg (1119−31)/(44×57) = 0.4338.
findings.actual: "H001 counted in Heifers; Heifers: head=45 adg=0.4363 ..."
findings.consequence: An animal already sorted off can still be judged against the wrong target and listed in a 'pull and check these animals' row for a group it no longer runs with, sending the crew to look in the wrong herd.
findings.regression_test: GN-10 data: assert H001 is in Cows (or in a 'changed group' list), and Heifers head = 44 with adg about 0.4338 (1088/2508 by hand).
findings.proposed_fix: Use the latest row's group (b.group) for where the animal is now, and list animals whose group changed within the period.

findings.title: Wording: 'since <date>' hides that the period ended at the last weigh-in; the slow list has no dates; '1 yearlings'; 1.598 shown as '1.60'
findings.location: exceptions.js:131 and 135-136; app.js:56 (tile 'since Jul 20'), app.js:209 and index.html:94 ('since the last weigh-in')
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/gain.repro.mjs, cases GN-21 and GB-C1. (a) The committed data. (b) Five of the six slow yearlings moved to an unknown group, leaving one slow animal. (c) One yearling gaining 159.8 lbs over 100 days (1.598).
findings.expected: (a) The text names the period end ('Jul 20 to Sep 15 weigh-ins'). (b) Subject '1 yearling'. (c) A displayed figure visibly under the 1.6 line, for example '1.598'.
findings.actual: "(a) 0.44 lbs/day since 2026-07-20 vs 1.0 target || (b) subject '1 yearlings' || (c) serious | 1.60 lbs/day since 2026-06-01 vs 2.0 target". GB-C1: tile "Yearling gain / 1.94 lbs/day / target 2.0, since Jul 20", heading "Daily gain since the last weigh-in".
findings.consequence: On Sep 30, 'since Jul 20' reads as 'through today', but the figure ended Sep 15. 'Since the last weigh-in' describes a period after Sep 15 that was never measured. These small slips hurt credibility in a portfolio piece aimed at operations roles.
findings.regression_test: Assert the committed heifer problem contains 'Sep 15' or '09-15'. Assert one slow animal gives the subject '1 yearling'. Assert a group at 1.598 shows a figure below 1.60, or the words 'under 1.6'.
findings.proposed_fix: Word it as '0.44 lbs/day between the Jul 20 and Sep 15 weigh-ins (target 1.0)'. Add the period to the slow-animal row. Fix the plural. Retitle the chart 'Daily gain between the last two weigh-ins'. Show enough decimals near the threshold.

checked_ok: Committed-data gain figures are correct and match a separate Python calculation (each animal's Jul 20 and Sep 15 weights looked up, then pooled). Heifers 1119/2565 = 0.436257; Yearlings 16608/8550 = 1.942456; slow yearlings ['Y027','Y031','Y058','Y082','Y129','Y132']. GN-C1 MATCH: "serious | Heifers | 0.44 lbs/day since 2026-07-20 vs 1.0 target  ||  warning | 6 yearlings | Under 1.0 lbs/day: Y027, Y031, Y058, Y082, Y129, Y132".

Mean of per-animal ADG equals the pooled gain when all animals share one weigh period (the committed data). GN-C2 MATCH: "Heifers: head=45 adg=0.4363 from=2026-07-20 to=2026-09-15; Yearlings: head=150 adg=1.9425 ...". The two methods only diverge when intervals differ (see the one-day re-weigh finding).

Thresholds are strict 'under' at exactly 80% and 50%. GN-C3 MATCH: "at80: (no Gain rows) ## under80: serious | Yearlings | 1.58 lbs/day ... ## at50: (no Gain rows) ## under50: warning | 1 yearlings | Under 1.0 lbs/day: A".

Negative group gain is flagged serious with the correct sign. GN-C4 MATCH: "serious | Heifers | -0.53 lbs/day since 2026-07-20 vs 1.0 target". The chart draws a negative axis: GB-C2 MATCH, "gridlines=9 labels=[\"avg -0.53\",...]; ticks=-1.0,-0.5,0.0,0.5,1.0,1.5,2.0,2.5,3.0".

The page renders the gain section correctly on the committed data. GB-C1 MATCH: "pageerrors=[]; tiles=5; exception rows=10; gain chart=true dots=195 (NaN cx: 0) gridlines=7 labels=[\"avg 0.44\",\"target 1.0\",\"avg 1.94\",\"target 2.0\"]; yearling tile=\"Yearling gain / 1.94 lbs/day / target 2.0, since Jul 20\"".

Suppressing the per-animal list when the whole group is flagged works as documented. On the committed data 32 of 45 heifers are under 0.5 (Python), yet only the serious Heifers row is shown. The rules table text is 'Animals under 50% of target (skipped when the whole group is already flagged)'.
Date sorting is correct for the ISO YYYY-MM-DD dates the generator writes: every animal's period is 2026-07-20 to 2026-09-15 (GN-C2).
The data stays labelled fictional in the page header. GB-C1 as-of text begins "Example Ranch (fictional), 4,300 acres".
The existing test suite passes: `node --test tests/exceptions.test.mjs` printed '# tests 8 / # pass 8 / # fail 0'. It covers only the planted gain outcomes and the head counts [45, 150].
